text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Block(x, y) ::: x can block shooting from y.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.

Premises:
∀x ∀y (Man(x) ∧ Man(y) ∧ Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
∀x (Taller(x, Michael) ∧ ∀y (Taller(y, x) → y = Michael)) ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y and y is taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Peter(t) ∧ Taller(t, Michael) ::: Peter is a man who is taller than Michael.
Michael can block any shooting from a person if that person does not jump when shooting.
¬Jump(Windy) ::: Windy cannot jump when shooting.
∀x (CanShoot(x) ∧ Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump is a great shooter.
Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.

Conclusion:
∃x (Man(x) ∧ Taller(x, Michael)) ::: There exists a man taller than Michael.
Peter is shorter than some man in Michael's class.
